Junior Doctors Need Life Support

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Junior doctors have blamed the government's lack of planning for the emotional roller coaster they faced about starting their compulsory community service. Although most S.A born junior doctors have been placed in public hospitals, the future remains unclear for foreign graduates with permanent residency in SA. With the mid year application process opening soon , just under 200 junior doctors have still not been placed.


Summary:
The constant failure by government and provinces to adequately fund internship and community service placements for graduating health professionals represents a serious human resource challenge as well as ethical disquiet. The issue stems from a lack of funded posts and insufficient accredited hospitals to host and train medical graduates. Minister Motsoaledi blamed the lack of foresight and planning for the shortage of junior doctor posts. The national health department oversees the process, but it depends on provinces who runt the hospitals to create an fund the posts, Most of the unplaced applicants are foreign graduates hoping to join the SA workforce.
Many hospitals are currently understaffed. In KZN Manguzi, Mosveld, Umphumulo, Stanger and Untunjabili are just a few facing doctor shortages affecting patient
care and placing increasingly heavy burdens on the remaining staff. Why then are so many junior doctors forced to sit at home? Until they have completed their community year they are not employable as doctors in SA. The government has legislated that junior doctors do community service but now many are forced into unemployment and not able to complete their training.

Further information:
There is grave concern among Medical Deans about the future of academic medicine because of chronic underfunding of health professional education and training. The absence of a national integrated and comprehensive health system plan,poor human resource planning and poor governance and management of the health system continues to destabilize academic health services.
There are serious doubts whether team running the placements system by the Department of Health is adequately equipped to run a complex system of placement sustainability.
It seems to elude the department that it is imperative that graduates be placed as their services are critical to the functioning of the health care system. They do all the frontline work.

Press Release:


Young Doctor Crisis
Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, has admitted that the public health system is ‘seriously distressed’ and confirmed that many medical posts are vacant, despite an ‘avalanche of patients’. But in the face of the human resource crisis, scores of newly qualified young doctors are sitting at home unemployed. Carte Blanche challenges the Department of Health about the planning, policies and processes that are failing the young doctors whose training has cost tax payers millions of rands, and whose lives now depend on their deployment.

metadata.Summary: The constant failure by government and provinces to adequately fund internship and community service placements for graduating health professionals represents a serious human resource challenge as well as ethical disquiet. The issue stems from a lack of funded posts and insufficient accredited hospitals to host and train medical graduates. Minister Motsoaledi blamed the lack of foresight and planning for the shortage of junior doctor posts. The national health department oversees the process, but it depends on provinces who runt the hospitals to create an fund the posts, Most of the unplaced applicants are foreign graduates hoping to join the SA workforce. Many hospitals are currently understaffed. In KZN Manguzi, Mosveld, Umphumulo, Stanger and Untunjabili are just a few facing doctor shortages affecting patient care and placing increasingly heavy burdens on the remaining staff. Why then are so many junior doctors forced to sit at home? Until they have completed their community year they are not employable as doctors in SA. The government has legislated that junior doctors do community service but now many are forced into unemployment and not able to complete their training.
metadata.Further information: There is grave concern among Medical Deans about the future of academic medicine because of chronic underfunding of health professional education and training. The absence of a national integrated and comprehensive health system plan,poor human resource planning and poor governance and management of the health system continues to destabilize academic health services. There are serious doubts whether team running the placements system by the Department of Health is adequately equipped to run a complex system of placement sustainability. It seems to elude the department that it is imperative that graduates be placed as their services are critical to the functioning of the health care system. They do all the frontline work.
